context: Each move climbs only 1 or 2 stairs. Let dp[n] be the number of ways to reach stair n, with initial values dp[1]=1 and dp[2]=2.
description: Stairs 3, 4, and 5 are highlighted in green, teal, and blue. Three dashed green paths reach stair 3 (labeled dp[3]=3), and five solid teal paths reach stair 4 (dp[4]=5). A dashed green arc over 2 stairs and a solid teal arc over 1 stair then reach stair 5. Above is dp[5]=dp[3]+dp[4]=8. Below, stairs 1 through 6 are paired with their counts.

frames.explanation: The final move to stair 5 climbs either 2 stairs from stair 3 or 1 from stair 4. Append a two-stair move to each of the 3 routes to stair 3 to get 3 routes to stair 5. Append a one-stair move to each of the 5 routes to stair 4 to get 5 more. The starting stairs of the last moves differ, so the groups are disjoint and cover all possibilities. Thus dp[5]=dp[3]+dp[4]=3+5=8. For any stair i (i≥3), the same reasoning gives dp[i]=dp[i-1]+dp[i-2].
frames.title: Adding the counts for stairs 3 and 4 gives the count for stair 5

summary: The last move to stair 5 must start at stair 3 or 4, so the number of ways is 3+5=8.
title: Adding the counts for stairs 3 and 4 gives the count for stair 5
